# Q-053: a_usd_deposit_on_a_holding_account_and_its_fee_as_its_own_transaction.txt
# as the owner books it once they know the deposit was the customer paying
# INV-USD-1.
#
# The holding-account amount is the receivable settling the invoice, at the
# 3,791.14 it was posted at, and the deposit's `$residual$` split states what
# the collection realizes, -24.75. The fee is its own transaction still: the
# 1.01 is the bank charge, and the 0.72 comes out of the invoice's cost basis,
# `{invoice_posting}` in this file, which the test fills in with that split's
# guid, valued at what it costs, 1.00. Its `$residual$` split states -0.01.
# Imported with `--strategy update`, beside INV-USD-1's `payment:` block
# stating the deposit and its receivable split.
#
# The deposit's new version establishes no cost basis, since the dollars'
# cost is the invoice's, so the fee's old version draws on a cost basis the
# book will no longer have. Only the finished book, with the fee's new
# version in it, has every draw on a cost basis that exists.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_an_atomic_import_brings_a_book_back_to_a_state_it_exported.py.
2026-08-13 * "Received money from Example Customer Inc"
	guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000c01"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Wise USD 2720.00 USD
		guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000c02"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "3815.89"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD -2720.00 USD
		guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000c03"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "-3791.14"
	Income:FX gain $residual$ CAD
2026-08-13 * "Transfer fee"
	guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000d01"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Bank charges 1.01 CAD
		guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000d02"
	Assets:Wise USD -0.72 USD
		guid: "0e530000000000000000000000000d03"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "-1.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{invoice_posting}"
	Income:FX gain $residual$ CAD
